sources.readScope: Selected primary passages were actually displayed and inspected with their proofs, neighboring claims and scholia as itemized below. The whole work was downloaded, not read continuously.
inspectedBlocks: Part I Definitions 1–8 and Axioms 1–7; Propositions 1–7; Proposition 11 including alternative proofs and scholium; Propositions 12–18 including corollaries and scholia; Propositions 24–33 (P33 first proof); Propositions 34–36; Appendix.

Part II Preface, Definitions 1–7 and Axioms; Propositions 1–7 and scholia; Proposition 8 through corollary (scholium only partially inspected); Propositions 11–13 and physical interlude through Lemmas 1–7 (Lemma 7 scholium partially inspected); Propositions 16–18 including scholia; Propositions 35–42 including P40 scholia; P43 proposition and opening proof only; Propositions 44–46; P47 proof and opening scholium.

Part III Preface, Definitions 1–3, Postulates; Propositions 1–3 (P2 scholium not fully inspected); Propositions 4–11 including scholia; Propositions 58–59 including scholium; Definitions of the Emotions 1–3 and beginning explanation.
Part IV Preface and Definitions 1–8, Axiom; Propositions 2–7; Propositions 14–15; Proposition 18 and scholium; Propositions 23–28; Propositions 35–38 and scholia; Propositions 45–46 and scholia.

Part V Preface, Axioms and Propositions 1–6 with scholia; Proposition 10 and selected scholium paragraphs on preparation, hatred, fear and ambition; Propositions 14–42 with their proofs, scholia and corollaries. P7 and P13 were also partly or incidentally displayed but not relied upon as separately completed readings.

sources.author: Steven Nadler
sources.title: Baruch Spinoza

boundedExcerptsInspected.quote: There is some debate in the literature as to whether God is also to be identified with Natura naturata.
He knows that the soul is not immortal in any personal sense, but is endowed only with a certain kind of eternity.

contextNotes: Section 2.1 reconstructs I.P5/I.P11/I.P14, discusses inherence versus causality and identifies rival uses of pantheism. Nadler favors identifying God with both productive and produced Nature and argues against worshipful interpretation. This is attributed interpretation, not consensus.
Sections 2.2–2.3 discuss causal closure of attributes, identity of body and idea and adequacy; II.P37 gives a caution against collapsing common properties into singular essence.

Sections 2.4–2.5 connect naturalism to conatus, adequate causation, active affect and social benefit, and interpret intellectual love and eternity nonpersonally. The article does not settle the specialist eternity disputes raised in PH-S04.

sources.author: Michael LeBuffe
sources.title: Spinoza’s Psychological Theory
inspectedSections: 1.1 The Argument to the Striving Doctrine
1.2 The Striving Doctrine as an Account of the Natures of Particular Objects
1.3 The Striving Doctrine as an Account of Human Nature
3.1 Good and Evil as Modes of Thinking

boundedExcerptsInspected.quote: Why is it that, just because a thing does not strive to destroy itself, that thing must therefore strive to persevere in being?
Spinoza is a predominant, not an orthodox, egoist.

contextNotes: Section 1.1 distinguishes not striving to persevere from striving not to persevere and examines how I.P25c/I.P34 address the possibility of inactive things. It leaves a pressure between inertia and motivational conatus.
Section 1.2 examines individuation, destruction and examples of apparently self-destructive composites.
Section 1.3 distinguishes always consciously selfish agents from predominantly self-preserving agents, and weighs III.P9 against IV.P20 and IV.P44s. This complicates Nadler’s general egoism label.
Sections 3.1–3.2 distinguish describing evaluations from the normative account of good and perfection; reconciling model-based perfection and reality-based perfection remains difficult.
limits: Section 2 on affects and the cited secondary books/articles were not independently read.
A secondary locator in the article appears as IVp36s2; it was not adopted. Primary social-state discussion is verified at IV.P37s2 in Elwes.
Full copyrighted retrieval is not distributed; bounded quotes and paraphrases retain inspected evidence.
